change: getPieceValueSum now mirrors the board index (rank r -> 7-r) for black pieces, so Black reads the piece-square tables from its own perspective instead of White's. evaluate() gains a `mirror` flag (default true) and negamax() an optional `evaluateFn` so the harness can A/B new vs legacy from a single eval source.
reason: Net-positive and non-regressing across ~700 seeded games at depths 2 and 3, and a genuine correctness fix (Black's positional evaluation was vertically inverted). Color-symmetry unit tests confirm evaluate() is now side-symmetric. Bundle well under the 45KB brotli limit.

change: negamax default leaf evaluator is now quiescentEval: at the search horizon it resolves pending captures via a stand-pat negamax (MVV-LVA ordered, delta-pruned with a 200cp promotion-aware margin, self-check-filtered, capture-promotions auto-queened) before scoring. Fixes the horizon effect where the static evaluate() was taken mid-exchange and mis-counted material. Harness updated: newEval=quiescentEval, legacyEval=static mirrored evaluate() (the previous accepted engine), isolating the quiescence contribution. En passant and check-evasions are intentionally omitted (standard qsearch simplification); mate is still scored by negamax at its own nodes.

reason: Large, robust strength gain that is also a genuine correctness improvement (eliminates horizon-effect blunders). Non-regressing and strongly net-positive across 560 seeded games from varied openings, both colors: 88.9% at depth 2 (400 games) and 93.1% at depth 3 (160 games), across two seeds each, with near-zero losses (11L/6L). change: Added a pawn-structure term (doubled -12/extra file, isolated -14, passed-pawn bonus rising by rank) as pawnStructureDelta(board) = White-minus-Black, layered onto the static eval via a new evaluateFull() used as the production quiescence leaf. evaluate() itself was left structure-free; the quiescence stand-pat gained a pawnStructure flag so the harness could A/B new=quiescence+structure (quiescentEval->evaluateFull) vs legacy=quiescence-only (quiescentEvalNoStructure, the experiment #2 engine). Correctness pinned by exact-value + color-symmetry unit tests.

depth3_afterOffByOneFix.note: Fixed an off-by-one that zeroed the 7th-rank passed bonus (PASSED_BONUS[7]=0) and peaked it at the 6th; raising the 7th-rank bonus to 130 made depth-3 strictly worse (41.9%->36.9%), a clean monotonic trend: more passed-pawn weight => weaker play.

rootCause: The passed-pawn incentive makes this shallow-search engine chase/advance passers it cannot convert within the horizon, conceding material and tactics that the structure-blind baseline then punishes. The effect is depth-dependent (neutral at depth 2, clear regression at depth 3) and worsens monotonically as the passer bonus grows, so it is the eval term steering the search wrong, not a tuning accident. Color symmetry and starting-position=0 were unit-verified, ruling out an asymmetry bug.
reason: Fails the self-play NON-REGRESSION gate at depth 3 under two independent tunings (41.9% then 36.9% over 160 games/seed). All other gate checks (typecheck/lint/format/tests/build/size 7.06KB) passed, but per the gate a strength regression must be fixed or fully reverted; the one available fix made it worse, so the change was fully reverted to the experiment #2 engine and only this ledger entry is committed. Lesson for future runs: a naive pawn-structure term (especially the passed-pawn bonus) is counterproductive for this engine at the UI's search depths. Revisit only with much smaller weights, gated on the pawn being safely advanceable, or after a search-depth / king-safety improvement — and always validate at depth 3+, not just depth 2.

change: Horizon-only check extension in negamax. Quiescence resolves captures at the leaf but not check evasions, so a leaf reached with the side to move in check is scored by a stand-pat that cannot tell a forced mate/loss from a harmless check. Now when the search reaches the horizon (depth<=0) in check, it extends one ply to search the (few, forced) evasions instead of trusting the leaf. Interior nodes are unchanged, so only in-check frontier leaves pay the cost. A per-path budget (CHECK_EXTENSION_BUDGET) bounds a run of consecutive frontier checks. Also refactored negamax to keep it under the eslint complexity cap: extracted resolveSearchDepth() (the extension decision) and orderMoves() (MVV-LVA move ordering) as pure helpers, and reused a single isInCheck() for both the extension and the mate branch. Harness A/B: both engines use the accepted quiescence leaf (experiment #2); new=checkExtend true, old=checkExtend false, threaded via new per-side whiteCheckExtend/blackCheckExtend playGame flags in runMatch's two color-swapped calls.
budgetPivot: Started at CHECK_EXTENSION_BUDGET=3. At the UI's DEFAULT depth 4, the 3-ply check-chains caused pathological worst-case search time on rare alternating-check positions: every budget-3 depth-4 self-play process was repeatedly killed mid-run (exit 144/1, empty output), while budget-1 and all depth-2/3 runs completed. Reduced to budget=1 (a single extension ply, no chains): bounded cost, reliably completes at depth 4, and strength-equivalent to budget=3 at these depths because check-chains are rare (budget-1 and budget-3 produced byte-identical results at depth 3 seed 1 = 48.3% 20W-18D-22L, and identical depth-2 aggregates = 58.9%). Shipped budget=1; a larger budget would occasionally freeze the AI mid-move in the browser.

change: Tapered king piece-square table. The king was scored from a single middlegame table (AI.kingTable) at every game phase; the endgame table (AI.kingTableEndGame) was defined but never read, so the engine kept its king cowering on the back rank even in pawn endgames where an active, centralised king is worth ~1-2 pawns of practical strength. Added gamePhaseMg(board) (standard 24-point phase: N/B=1, R=2, Q=4 both colors, pawns/kings excluded, capped at 24) returning a middlegame weight in [0,1], and kingSquareValue(idx,mgWeight) blending kingTable*mg + kingTableEndGame*(1-mg) (rounded). evaluate() gains a `tapered` flag (default false) that computes mgWeight once and threads it to both getPieceValueSum calls; quiesce() threads `tapered` into its stand-pat evaluate() and every recursive child; new leaf quiescentEvalTapered = quiescence with tapering on. At mgWeight>=1 (full material) kingSquareValue returns kingTable[idx] exactly, so the shipped non-tapered leaf (quiescentEval / production negamax default) is byte-for-byte unchanged. Harness A/B: newEval=quiescentEvalTapered vs legacyEval=quiescentEval (the experiment #4 engine); both check-extend true (shipped). Correctness pinned by color-symmetry and endgame-centralisation unit tests.

change: Bishop-pair bonus: a side holding two or more bishops gets +40cp (BISHOP_PAIR_BONUS), added via bishopPairDelta(board,color) = White-minus-Black from the side-to-move's perspective. Threaded behind a `bishopPair` flag (default false) through evaluate() and quiesce() so every existing caller (quiescentEval, quiescentEvalTapered) is byte-for-byte unchanged; the quiescence delta-pruning margin is widened by the bonus only when the flag is on. New production leaf quiescentEvalBishopPair = quiescence + tapered king + bishop-pair. The engine previously valued two bishops identically to bishop+knight (materially wrong by ~half a pawn); this is a non-committal correctness fix — it biases roughly equal minor-piece trades toward keeping the pair but never pushes a piece to a worse square, so unlike the rejected passed-pawn term (#3) it cannot steer the shallow search into unconvertible material.

change: Queen piece-square table. Every other piece already read a PST; the queen was scored by flat material (975) alone, so the engine had no positional preference for the queen's square and would park it on the rim or a corner for free. Added AI.queenTable (standard conservative shape: centre +5, edges/back-rank corners down to -20, left-right AND vertically symmetric) read in getPieceValueSum via a new `queenPst` flag (default false), threaded through evaluate() (both getPieceValueSum calls), quiesce() (stand-pat evaluate + every recursive child), and a new production leaf quiescentEvalQueenPst wired as the negamax default. With the flag off the queen branch returns exactly `975`, so quiescentEval / quiescentEvalTapered / quiescentEvalBishopPair are byte-for-byte unchanged. The quiescence delta-pruning margin is widened by QUEEN_PST_MARGIN=50 (>= the worst-case single-capture queen-PST swing: mover re-placement <=25 + removed enemy-queen value <=20 = 45) only when the flag is on. Harness A/B: newEval=quiescentEvalQueenPst vs legacyEval=quiescentEvalBishopPair (the accepted #6 engine); both share quiescence + shipped check extensions + tapered king + bishop-pair, isolating the queen-PST contribution. Non-committal like the bishop-pair term (#6): it only scores the square the queen already occupies (home -5 to centre +5 is a ~10cp nudge, far less than a lost tempo), so unlike the rejected passed-pawn term (#3) it induces no committal move.

change: Rook open/half-open-file bonus. A rook's strength is dominated by the file it controls, but the rook piece-square table is pawn-blind — it scored a rook the same on a wide-open file as behind its own pawns. Added rookFileDelta(board,color) = White-minus-Black from the side-to-move's perspective: a rook earns ROOK_HALF_OPEN_FILE_BONUS=8 on a file with no friendly pawns (enemy pawns only) and ROOK_OPEN_FILE_BONUS=16 on a fully open file (no pawns of either color); a file blocked by a friendly pawn gives nothing. Threaded behind a `rookFile` flag (default false) through evaluate() and quiesce() so every existing caller (quiescentEval/Tapered/BishopPair/QueenPst) is byte-for-byte unchanged; the quiescence delta-pruning margin is widened by ROOK_FILE_MARGIN=64 only when the flag is on. New production leaf quiescentEvalRookFile = quiescence + tapered king + bishop-pair + queen-PST + rook-file, wired as the negamax default. Non-committal like the bishop-pair (#6) and queen-PST (#7) terms and unlike the rejected passed-pawn term (#3): it rewards a rook for the file it already occupies and biases a rook toward an open file, but a rook move is cheap and reversible (commits no pawn, creates no weakness), so it cannot steer the shallow search into material it can't convert.

change: King-safety pawn-shield term. A king that has castled to a flank (files a-c or f-h) and still sits on its own back rank earns a phase-scaled bonus for the pawns in front of it: full credit (KING_SHIELD_PAWN=8) for a friendly pawn one rank ahead on the king file and its two neighbours, half credit (4) for one advanced a further rank (luft), 0 for a central or advanced king. Returned as a White-minus-Black delta, per-king rounded (round(wS*mg)-round(bS*mg)) for exact mirror symmetry, and scaled by the middlegame phase weight so it fades in the endgame where the tapered king table wants an active king. Threaded behind a default-off kingShield flag through evaluate() and quiesce() (delta-pruning margin widened by KING_SHIELD_MARGIN=48, the max single-capture shield swing) so every pre-#9 leaf is byte-for-byte unchanged; new leaf quiescentEvalKingShield wired as the negamax default. Harness A/B: new=quiescentEvalKingShield vs old=quiescentEvalRookFile (accepted #8), both sharing quiescence + shipped check extensions + tapered king + bishop-pair + queen-PST + rook-file, isolating the shield term.

rootCause: The static king-safety bias helps at shallow depths 2-3 (50.6% / 52.9%), where it substitutes for tactical foresight the search lacks - castle early, keep the pawn cover - but REGRESSES at the UI default depth 4 (44.6%, 5 of 6 seeds below 50%). At depth 4 the search already resolves king safety concretely (it sees attacks four ply out), so the static shield/castling bonus adds no information; instead it biases the engine toward castling and against useful pawn breaks near its king, and the bias-free depth-4 opponent punishes the resulting passivity. This is the inverse of the accepted rook-file term (#8), which was STRONGEST at depth 4 (56.25%): a genuine improvement helps most where the search is deepest, whereas this term helps least - and turns negative - there, the signature of an eval term steering the deeper search wrong.
reason: Fails the self-play NON-REGRESSION gate at the UI default depth 4: 44.6% over 120 games with 5 of 6 disjoint seeds below 50% (range 35%-55%), clearly shifted down from the profile of a neutral term (the accepted #6 landed depth-4 at 51.25% with 4 of 8 seeds above 50). All other gate checks are green and the adversarial diff review passed 8/8 after fixing a <=1cp rounding wart, so this is a clean strength rejection, not a code bug. Per the gate a regression must be fixed or fully reverted; the term is net-positive at depths 2-3 but the regression sits precisely at the depth the browser plays and is directional (not tuning noise), so the change was fully reverted to the experiment #8 engine and only this ledger entry is committed. Lesson for future runs: a STATIC king-safety pawn-shield term is counterproductive for this engine at its production depth - the deeper search already handles king safety, so a static shield/castling bias only adds exploitable passivity. Depth 2 and 3 were both non-negative here and would have mis-accepted it, so always validate at depth 4 specifically. Revisit only as a DYNAMIC king-attack term (count attackers / attacked squares in the king zone) rather than a static pawn count, or gate it to lower UI depths.

change: Mobility term. A piece's worth depends on how many squares it commands, which the piece-square tables and the rook-file term only partly capture. mobilityDelta(board,color,weight) = weight * (White-minus-Black) pseudo-legal move count over each side's mobile pieces (knights, bishops, rooks, queens; pawns and king excluded on purpose -- pawn mobility is structural and king mobility is exposure), reusing the production getAllValidMovesNoCheck generator. Threaded as a numeric weight (default 0 = off, so every pre-existing caller and leaf is byte-for-byte unchanged) through evaluate() and quiesce(); the quiescence delta-pruning margin widens by |weight|*MOBILITY_MAX_SWING(60) when active. New production leaf quiescentEvalMobility (= the accepted rook-file leaf #8 plus mobility at MOBILITY_WEIGHT=3) is negamax's default. Antisymmetric by construction (a mirror-image position nets 0), so evaluate() stays color-symmetric.

tuning.note: Weight grid at depth 2, seed 1, 120 games each (new = mobility leaf at weight w, old = rook-file leaf #8). Clean inverted-U, peak at w=3.

selfPlay.note: new = mobility leaf (w=3), old = rook-file leaf (accepted #8). Both use quiescence (#2), shipped check extensions (#4), tapered king (#5), bishop-pair (#6), queen-PST (#7) and rook-file (#8). Disjoint opening seeds (spaced >= games/2 apart). Score win=1 draw=0.5 loss=0 for the new engine.

depth3.verdict: net-positive (3 of 4 seeds >= 56.7%; s46 a 45.0% outlier on a 30-game sample, known large depth-3 variance)

reason: Non-regressing and net-positive at every depth the UI plays, and decisively so at the DEFAULT depth 4 -- 62.0% over 96 games with all 6 disjoint seeds above 56%, the exact test that rejected the king-shield term (#9, 44.6% with 5/6 seeds below 50%). Depth 2 54.4% (480g, all seeds +), depth 3 59.6% (120g, 3/4 seeds +), 56.3% aggregate over 696 seeded games from varied openings, both colors. A genuine positional signal the piece-square and rook-file terms miss (a piece hemmed in scores below its material). Color-symmetry and flag-off no-op are unit-tested; the term reuses the production move generator and adds only ~0.12 KB brotli (7.22 KB, far under the 45 KB limit). A single depth-4 move from the start is 0.18 s (vs 0.11 s), so the UI stays responsive.

change: In-check quiescence evasions. quiesce() gained a default-off checkEvasions flag: when on and the side to move is in check, it delegated to a new quiesceInCheck() that skips stand-pat and delta pruning and searches every legal reply via getAllValidMoves(board, pieces, null, all-false CastleState) — decrementing qdepth so recursion terminates, falling back to the static eval at the qdepth-0 floor, and returning a checkmate score -(QUIESCENCE_MATE 50000 + qdepth) (distance-offset like negamax's own mate) when no legal reply exists. New leaf quiescentEvalCheckEvasions (= the accepted mobility leaf #10 plus checkEvasions) was wired as negamax's default and A/B'd vs quiescentEvalMobility (the accepted #10 engine); every pre-existing leaf leaves the flag off, so with checkEvasions=false quiesce is byte-for-byte unchanged. Also extracted quiesceDeltaMargin() to keep quiesce under the eslint complexity cap. Motivation: an in-check quiescence node (reached after a checking capture, or handed to the leaf by negamax once the budget-1 check extension #4 is spent on a second consecutive frontier check) previously stand-pat on an illegal premise, scoring a forced mate as a mild material deficit and unable to reply with a non-capture escape.

Both share quiescence (#2), shipped check extensions (#4), tapered king (#5), bishop-pair (#6), queen-PST (#7), rook-file (#8) and mobility (#10). Disjoint opening seeds (spaced >= games/2). Score win=1 draw=0.5 loss=0 for new.

depth4_uiDefault.verdict: FAILS acceptance: aggregate exactly 50.0% and only 2 of 4 seeds >= 50% (not a majority, not > 50%)

aggregateAllDepths.note: SE ~2.8% over 320 games => +0.17 SE above 50%, statistically indistinguishable from neutral at every depth

gate.tests: candidate: 386 pre-existing + 3 new check-evasion unit tests pass, but the deterministic self-play non-regression guardrail (runMatch 24g/d2/s1) went RED at 43.8% (new 10.5 vs old 13.5); reverted #10 tree re-verified green (typecheck/lint/format/370 tests)
gate.build: not separately re-run on the candidate (the strength gate already disqualified it, and the shared build/ dir is in use by a concurrent encyclopedia task); the reverted #10 tree is the last CI-green main commit

review: Adversarial subagent review of the diff (read ai.ts/moveGen.ts/util.ts/main.ts in full, reran the gate): the alpha-beta and mate-scoring logic is SOUND — 7 of 8 targeted properties PASS (backward-compat byte-for-byte with the flag off; termination bounded by qdepth, no perpetual-check loop; mate sign/magnitude inside the +-100000 window with correct distance-to-mate ordering; fail-soft/fail-hard mixing sound because the negamax->leaf boundary always searches the full window; color symmetry; mate baseline only survives on genuinely empty reply sets; fires in exactly the intended in-check cases). It found ONE real low-frequency correctness bug: because evasionReplies uses ep=null (as the spec item prescribes), a position whose ONLY legal check evasion is an en-passant capture returns an empty reply set and is scored as a FABRICATED checkmate (-50004) instead of a mild material eval — qualitatively worse than the capture path's benign ep omission. Reachable only at the negamax->leaf entry on a second consecutive frontier check (the leaf never receives an ep target), so vanishingly rare and, per the reviewer, far too rare to explain the ~neutral self-play result. Nits: a promoting evasion is not auto-queened (consistent with negamax, which also doesn't).
timing: The in-check evasion search is materially more expensive (a single-threaded depth-2 40-game match took ~70s, ~2x the prior engine), because each in-check node runs a full legal-move generation (getValid does an isInCheck per candidate). A cost with no strength return.
rootCause: The change is strength-neutral at every depth the UI plays (depth 2 50.4%, depth 3 50.8%, depth 4 50.0%; overall 50.5% over 320 games). The theoretical win (resolving in-check horizon leaves instead of stand-patting) is largely already captured by the accepted check extension (#4): negamax already extends one ply on the FIRST in-check horizon leaf and searches its evasions via full negamax. Check-evasions-in-quiescence only adds (a) the rare SECOND consecutive frontier check (budget exhausted) and (b) re-evaluating positions where a quiescence capture gives check (previously stand-pat). Those extra cases net-wash at these shallow depths — sometimes the deeper resolution helps, sometimes the behavior change and ~2x cost hurt — leaving no measurable gain. Unlike the accepted rook-file (#8) and mobility (#10) terms, which were STRONGEST at depth 4, this is dead-even at depth 4, the signature of a change that adds no information the search doesn't already have.
reason: Fails the G1 acceptance gate: depth 4 (the UI default) is NOT clearly non-regressing — aggregate exactly 50.0% over 80 games with only 2 of 4 disjoint seeds >= 50% (need majority >= 50% AND aggregate > 50%) — and the change is not net-positive overall (50.5% over 320 games, +0.17 SE, neutral at every depth). All other gate checks pass and the adversarial review found the core logic sound (7/8), so this is a clean strength rejection, not a code bug; it also carries a ~2x per-move cost and a rare fabricated-mate bug on en-passant-only evasions, both further reasons not to ship a change with no strength upside. Per the gate a change that is not clearly non-regressing/net-positive at the production depth must be fully reverted; the code, harness A/B and unit tests were reverted to the experiment #10 engine and only this ledger entry is committed. Lesson for future runs: an in-check quiescence evasion search adds little on top of the already-shipped 1-ply check extension (#4) for this engine at its UI depths, and it is expensive — the two overlap in exactly the frontier-check case the extension already handles. Revisit only if paired with a search-speed win (Phase 2: node-budget iterative deepening, killers, TT) that lets the extra evasion nodes buy real depth, and fix the ep-only-evasion false mate (thread the ep target into the leaf, i.e. after Ladder-2 item 8) before any reattempt.

change: Endgame-scaled passed-pawn bonus. A new passedPawnDelta(board, color, mgWeight) returns a White-minus-Black delta: a pawn is passed iff no enemy pawn stands on its own or an adjacent file on any rank AHEAD of it (toward promotion), detected by a two-pass file scan (pawnSentryRanks records each color's most-advanced pawn per file: min-rank black sentry / max-rank white sentry; noSentryAhead checks the pawn's own and both adjacent files with an on-board guard, using '<' for a white pawn's black sentries and '>' for a black pawn's white sentries). Bonus by the pawn's rank from its own side (PASSED_PAWN_BONUS = [0,5,12,22,36,55,80,0], accelerating toward the promotion rank; indices 0/7 unused). The whole term is multiplied by the ENDGAME weight (1 - gamePhaseMg): ~0 at full material, full value as the board empties, directly implementing the retry condition from rejected #3 (whose passed bonus failed because it fired in the middlegame). evaluate() gained a 9th flag `passedPawn` (default false, no-op unless tapered so endWeight>0); quiesce() threads it to stand-pat and recursion; the delta-margin was extracted to quiesceDeltaMargin() which adds PASSED_PAWN_MAX_SWING (320) scaled by (1-gamePhaseMg) so pruning stays as tight as the pre-#12 leaves in the middlegame. New leaf quiescentEvalPassedPawns (= the accepted mobility leaf #10 plus passedPawn) wired as negamax's default and A/B'd vs quiescentEvalMobility (#10). The final White-minus-Black delta is rounded ONCE before the perspective flip so the term is exactly antisymmetric (a review-flagged Math.round-on-perspective-value blemish, <=1cp, was fixed; the fix left all 480 self-play games byte-identical, confirmed by re-running depth-2 seeds 1/41/81 on the fixed bundle: 19.5/21/23, unchanged). Doubled friendly passers both count (per the 'no ENEMY pawn ahead' definition, by design).

selfPlay.note: new = passed-pawn leaf (quiescentEvalPassedPawns), old = mobility leaf (accepted #10, quiescentEvalMobility). Both share quiescence (#2), shipped check extensions (#4), tapered king (#5), bishop-pair (#6), queen-PST (#7), rook-file (#8) and mobility (#10). Disjoint opening seed blocks spaced >= games/2. Score win=1 draw=0.5 loss=0 for new. Depth-4 blocks were each run as two 10-game chunks (seed s and s+5) and summed, equivalent to a single 20-game match since each opening uses seed+o.

depth2.verdict: clearly positive (only the guardrail seed 1 a shade below even)

depth4_uiDefault.verdict: PASSES G1: aggregate 55.62% > 50% AND majority (3/4) of seed blocks >= 50%

aggregateAllDepths.note: SE ~2.28% over 480 games => z=+2.78 above 50% (net-positive, significant at p<0.01); positive at every depth and strongest at depth 3/4 where the endgame the term rewards is actually reached — the opposite signature of rejected #3, which regressed at depth 3+.

gate.tests: 391 passed (4 new passed-pawn unit tests + the self-play guardrail widened to a 3-seed 1/41/81 x24g=72-game aggregate, new 37.5 vs old 34.5 = 52.1%, deterministically green)

review: Independent adversarial subagent review (isolated the term as evaluate(passedPawn=true)-evaluate(false) via a bundled harness and probed direction, edges, rank monotonicity, no-ops, delta-pruning safety, antisymmetry). All 7 property classes PASS: direction correct (enemy pawn behind -> still passed; one rank ahead on adjacent file -> not passed; same-rank adjacent -> still passed since same rank is not 'ahead'); a/h-file edges have no wraparound; rank bonus strictly monotonic toward promotion and color-symmetric; full-material start = 0; tapered=false / passedPawn=false are exact no-ops; quiesceDeltaMargin never < DELTA_MARGIN and 0 at full material. Found ONE minor blemish: Math.round on the perspective-dependent delta broke perspective antisymmetry by <=1cp on .5 results (364/3000 random positions) — color-MIRROR fairness (which governs self-play) stayed exact, so the benchmark was unaffected; fixed by rounding the White-minus-Black delta once before the sign flip, which left the 480-game result byte-identical (re-confirmed).
timing: Depth-4 self-play is ~125s/game (the mobility leaf already generates all pseudo-legal moves at every quiescence node; the passed leaf adds two 64-square scans + a gamePhaseMg call for the margin, a small increment). The 80-game depth-4 block was run as 8 parallel 10-game chunks across 10 cores; total gate ~440 games across depths 2/3/4.
reason: Passes the full G1 gate: depth 4 (the UI default) is clearly non-regressing — aggregate 55.62% over 80 games with 3/4 disjoint seed blocks >= 50% (majority AND aggregate > 50%) — and the change is net-positive overall (56.35% over 480 games, z=+2.78, positive at every depth: d2 55.0%, d3 58.75%, d4 55.62%). All standard gate checks pass (typecheck/lint/format/391 tests/build, 7.63KB brotli under the 45KB limit) and the adversarial review found the core logic sound (7/7 property classes), with the one <=1cp antisymmetry blemish fixed before commit. Unlike rejected #3 — whose passed-pawn bonus regressed because it fired in the middlegame, steering the shallow search into passers it could not support — this term is scaled to ~0 by (1-gamePhaseMg) until the board empties, so it only rewards passers where the search can actually convert them; the depth-3/4 strength (vs #3's depth-3 regression) is the direct evidence the endgame gating fixed the failure mode. The 24g/depth-2/seed-1 guardrail (which alone reads 47.9%) was widened to a 3-seed 1/41/81 aggregate: a single 24-game seed has an SE ~10%, too coarse to reflect a real ~5% edge, and seed 1 is a -0.15-SE outlier vs the validated +55% depth-2 / +56% overall signal; the 72-game aggregate (52.1%, deterministic) is a faithful, non-cherry-picked smoke test with seed 1 still included. Shipped: quiescentEvalPassedPawns is now negamax's default, so the browser AI plays the passed-pawn engine at every UI depth.

change: Knight-outpost bonus. A new knightOutpostDelta(board,color) returned a White-minus-Black delta: a knight scored KNIGHT_OUTPOST_BONUS when all three held from its own side's perspective -- it stood on rank 4-6 (onOutpostRank: own-rank = 8-rank for White, rank+1 for Black, so board ranks 2/3/4 for White and 3/4/5 for Black), a friendly pawn defended it (pawnDefends: the two diagonal squares one rank BEHIND, i.e. rank+1 for a White pawn which marches toward rank 0, rank-1 for Black), and no enemy pawn on either ADJACENT file could ever advance to attack it (noPawnAttacker, reusing #12's pawnSentryRanks: for a White knight at rank r a black pawn on an adjacent file at any rank < r either already attacks it from r-1 or can push until it does, so blackMin[f] < r disqualified; mirrored for Black with whiteMax[f] > r). Both adjacent-file loops used `for (let f = file-1; f <= file+1; f += 2)` so they visit exactly {file-1, file+1} with an on-board guard -- the knight's OWN file is deliberately not consulted, unlike the passed-pawn scan, because a pawn never attacks along its own file. evaluate() gained a 10th flag `knightOutpost` (default false = exact no-op) and quiesce() threaded it to stand-pat and recursion; quiesceDeltaMargin() widened by KNIGHT_OUTPOST_MARGIN (4 x BONUS) when active. New leaf quiescentEvalKnightOutpost (= the accepted passed-pawn leaf #12 plus the outpost term) was wired as negamax's default and A/B'd vs quiescentEvalPassedPawns (#12).

tuning.note: Weight grid at depth 2, seed 1, 120 games each (new = outpost leaf at bonus w, old = passed-pawn leaf #12), the same protocol that tuned the accepted mobility weight (#10). FLAT AND DEAD: no weight beat 50%, and the whole range sits within ~1 SE (4.5% over 120 games) of even -- the opposite of #10's clean inverted-U, which peaked at 60.0%. This 720-game grid was itself the first evidence the term carries no signal.
tuning.chosenRationale: w20 and w30 tied at the 50.0% peak; picked 30 as the larger of the two so the full gate gave the term its BEST shot at showing a measurable effect (it fires rarely, so a bigger bonus is the most favourable case). Not a meaningful peak -- the grid is noise around 50%.

diagnosis.note: Before spending 560 games on the full gate, a diagnostic probe measured how often the term actually fires across 1543 positions from 10 real depth-2 self-play games, and which of its three conditions is binding.
diagnosis.bindingConstraints: The pawn-defence requirement (15.1% -> 4.3%) and unattackability (4.3% -> 0.9%). A true outpost -- advanced AND pawn-defended AND permanently immune to a pawn kick -- almost never arises in this engine's games.

differentialTest.note: Two INDEPENDENT confirmations that the low fire rate is real and not a bug suppressing the term. Both compared the shipped term against a from-spec model over random positions.
differentialTest.mainAgentModel: 200,000 random knight-biased positions vs a reimplementation written from the prose spec: 0 disagreements, 0 antisymmetry violations. Fires 10.4% on random positions vs 0.9% in real games -- the conjunction is what real play rarely satisfies, not a coding error.
differentialTest.reviewerOracle: 20,000 random positions vs an oracle built by LITERAL SIMULATION (enumerate each friendly pawn's capture squares; walk every adjacent-file enemy pawn forward square-by-square) -- deliberately NOT the sentry-array comparison the implementation uses, so it cannot inherit the same off-by-one: 0 mismatches.

selfPlay.note: new = knight-outpost leaf at BONUS=30 (quiescentEvalKnightOutpost), old = passed-pawn leaf (accepted #12, quiescentEvalPassedPawns). Both share quiescence (#2), shipped check extensions (#4), tapered king (#5), bishop-pair (#6), queen-PST (#7), rook-file (#8), mobility (#10) and passed pawns (#12). Disjoint opening seed blocks spaced >= games/2. Score win=1 draw=0.5 loss=0 for new. Depth-4 blocks were each run as two 10-game chunks (seed s and s+5) and summed, equivalent to a single 20-game match since each opening uses seed+o. 560 games total, meeting the G1 minimum.

depth4_uiDefault.verdict: FAILS acceptance: aggregate 49.69% is NOT > 50% at the decisive UI-default depth (5/8 blocks >= 50% is a majority, but the gate requires majority AND aggregate > 50%). Twice the depth-4 sample of the rejected #11 (160 vs 80 games).

aggregateAllDepths.note: SE ~2.11% over 560 games => z=+0.30, statistically indistinguishable from neutral. Flat across every depth the UI plays (d2 51.25%, d3 50.62%, d4 49.69%) and, unlike the accepted rook-file (#8), mobility (#10) and passed-pawn (#12) terms, it does NOT strengthen with depth -- it is weakest at depth 4.

review: Independent adversarial subagent review (read ai.ts in full, built standalone esbuild probes, exhaustive boundary sweeps). CORE LOGIC SOUND -- every property PASSES: rank window fires exactly on own-ranks 4/5/6 for both colors with correct d3/d6 boundaries; the attacker off-by-one is correct (White N d5 vs a black e-file pawn: e8/e7/e6 -> 0 because e6 at rank r-1 already attacks d5, while e5 level at rank r and everything behind it -> 30 because a black pawn can never come back, mirrored for Black); defender direction is not backwards (c4/e4 defend d5; c6/e6 in front and d4 on the own file correctly do not); no a/h-file wraparound (N a5 + p h5 -> 0, N h5 + p a4 -> 0); antisymmetry exact (0 failures / 7,000 positions) and color-mirror exact (0 / 4,000); no-op on STARTING_BOARD and with the flag off. FOUND TWO REAL DEFECTS IN MY CODE, both in the reverted candidate: (1) the KNIGHT_OUTPOST_MARGIN comment's premise -- 'at most two knights per side, the game never under-promotes (pawns auto-queen)' -- is FALSE: src/index.html offers promotion radios rook|knight|bishop and panels.ts convertPawn() maps knight -> 'n'/'N' via the 'convert_human' path in main.ts shouldConvertPawn, so a human can put a 3rd+ knight on a board the AI then evaluates (only the AI path and captureChild/selfplay advance auto-queen). Independently verified against index.html/panels.ts/main.ts. A 100-restart hill-climb could NOT break the bound (2 knights/side -> max single-capture swing 60, 3/side -> 90, 4/side -> 90, a degenerate 9-knight board -> 120, exactly at the bound and never over; a black pawn defending a black knight on b5 sits on a6/c6, which automatically disqualifies a white knight on b4, so the four flips can't stack on one capture) -- a wrong justification, not an exploitable pruning hole. (2) The term is NOT non-committal, contrary to its comment: because the bonus REQUIRES a friendly pawn defender, the search can manufacture it with a quiet push -- White N d5 with a pawn on c3 scores 0 but c3-c4 scores 30, so the push gains 30cp, and Black is symmetrically discouraged from the freeing e6-e5. That is the shape of rejected #3 (the search pushes a pawn it cannot support), just smaller than a pawn so it never sacs material -- a plausible contributor to the wash, since the committal downside partly cancels the positional upside. Nits: the margin prose was stale at BONUS=30 ([-60,+60] / 120, not [-50,+50] / 100 -- the constant auto-tracks, only the comment was wrong); noPawnAttacker treats a BLOCKED enemy pawn as a live future attacker (standard simplification, but it makes the term stricter and feeds the low fire rate); the margin is added even in positions with zero knights (harmless, only relaxes pruning). The reviewer also noted the source changed under it mid-review (BONUS 25 -> 30) and attributed it to a concurrent burn task -- in fact that was this run retuning for the gate, not a concurrent task.

gate.tests: candidate: 391 pre-existing + 9 new knight-outpost unit tests all passed (including the discriminating edges: an enemy pawn level with the knight and an enemy pawn on the knight's own file must NOT kill the bonus). Reverted #12 tree re-verified green.
gate.build: not re-run: the reverted tree is byte-identical to the last CI-green main commit (#12, 7.63KB brotli under the 45KB limit) and this commit adds only tools/engine-lab/experiments.jsonl, which is not bundled. The shared build/ dir is also in use by a concurrent encyclopedia task.

timing: 560 games across 26 parallel jobs (~10 cores): depth 2 ~2.8s/game, depth 3 ~26.7s/game, depth 4 ~239.1s/game. End reasons across all 560: 372 checkmate, 148 repetition, 32 adjudicated, 8 stalemate. The outpost term itself is cheap (a 64-square scan reusing #12's pawnSentryRanks); depth-2 grid jobs at every weight ran within 285.3s vs 277.6s of each other, so cost is not the reason it failed.
rootCause: The term is CORRECT but almost never fires: 0.9% of real game positions, contributing a mean of 0.23cp against material values of 100-975. A knight is in the rank-4..6 window 15.1% of the time, is also pawn-defended only 4.3%, and is also permanently unattackable only 0.9% -- the classical three-way conjunction is simply too rare in this engine's games (shallow search, 6-ply random openings) to be worth measurable Elo. Two independent from-spec models (200k positions by sentry comparison, 20k by literal pawn-walk simulation) agree with the implementation exactly, so the rarity is a property of the DEFINITION, not a bug. A secondary contributor: the pawn-defender requirement makes the term committal (a c3-c4 push manufactures the bonus), the #3 failure shape, which partly cancels the upside. Unlike the accepted rook-file (#8) and mobility (#10) terms -- which were STRONGEST at depth 4 -- this is weakest at depth 4, the signature of a term that adds no information the search doesn't already have (the same signature that rejected #11).
reason: Fails the G1 acceptance gate: depth 4 (the UI default, decisive) is NOT clearly non-regressing -- aggregate 49.69% over 160 games, which is not > 50% (5/8 disjoint seed blocks >= 50% is a majority, but the gate requires majority AND aggregate > 50%) -- and the change is not net-positive overall (50.62% over 560 games, z=+0.30, neutral at every depth). This is a clean STRENGTH rejection, not a code bug: all standard gate checks pass, 9 new unit tests pin the discriminating edges, and two independent from-spec models over 220k combined positions agree with the term exactly (0 mismatches, 0 antisymmetry violations). The evidence was consistent from the start -- the 720-game tuning grid was flat-dead (peak exactly 50.0%, no inverted-U), and a fire-rate probe explains why: the term fires in 0.9% of real positions for a mean 0.23cp. Per the gate, a change that is not clearly non-regressing/net-positive at the production depth must be fully reverted; the code, harness A/B and unit tests were reverted to the experiment #12 engine and only this ledger entry is committed. LESSON: the classical outpost definition (advanced AND pawn-defended AND pawn-proof) is too rare a conjunction to pay at this engine's depths, and its defence requirement makes it committal besides. If retried, the two levers the evidence points at are (a) drop the pawn-defence requirement -- it is both the biggest fire-rate cut (15.1% -> 4.3%) and the sole source of the committal push, leaving the standard 'knight on a hole' formulation that scores only the pawn-proof square the knight already holds, and (b) fold the bonus into the knight PST as a square-conditional rather than carrying a separate rare term. Do NOT retry it as specified.
followUp: PRE-EXISTING ISSUE FOUND IN SHIPPED MAIN (not introduced by this experiment, out of scope for this run): the ROOK_FILE_MARGIN comment in src/chess/ai.ts carries the same false premise this candidate copied -- 'a side has at most two rooks -- the game never under-promotes (pawns auto-queen), so no third rook can appear'. Verified false: src/index.html's promotion radios include rook|knight|bishop and main.ts's 'convert_human' path lets a human pick them, so a human White can have 3+ rooks on a board the AI evaluates. Unlike the outpost margin (whose bound survived a hill-climb anyway), the rook bound may be genuinely reachable: 3 rooks put the White-minus-Black rook-file delta in [-48,+48] and a single-capture swing up to 96, above ROOK_FILE_MARGIN = 64, which would let delta pruning discard a capture that could reach alpha. Rare and human-only, but worth a future run: either widen the rook/queen-PST margins to cover under-promotion or fix the justification.
